guides.title: Half Dome permits (day hike)
guides.summary: You need a permit to go past the base of the subdome whenever the cables are up. It comes from the Half Dome lotteries; camping is a separate matter.

facts.label: When it applies
facts.text: Every day of the week, for anyone continuing above the base of the subdome toward the summit while the cables are up. Looking at Half Dome, or hiking only as far as Vernal or Nevada Fall, needs nothing.

facts.label: How to apply
facts.text: Enter a lottery on Recreation.gov (permit 234652) or by phone. Name a permit holder and, in the preseason lottery, an alternate; one of the two must be with the whole group at the subdome, where rangers check permits. Bring photo ID and the paid confirmation email. Permits are not transferable.

facts.label: Cost
facts.text: $10 per application, non-refundable, plus $10 per person awarded. The per-person fee comes back if you cancel by 11:59 pm Pacific the day before, or if the cables are down on your date. Two hikers on one application pay $30 in total.

facts.label: Lotteries
facts.text: Preseason: March 1 to 31 (Eastern time), results in mid-April, 225 day-hiker permits a day, up to six people per application. Daily, during cable season: apply two days before the hike between midnight and 4 pm Pacific, results late that night, permit holder only with no alternate. NPS caps the subdome at about 300 people a day: roughly 225 day hikers and 75 backpackers.

facts.label: Can I get one today?
facts.text: No. There is no same-day permit; while the cables are up you can enter today's daily lottery (before 4 pm Pacific) for a hike two days out. Entering does not reserve a place.

facts.label: Not included
facts.text: No camping or lodging. Backpackers, including anyone sleeping in Little Yosemite Valley, add Half Dome to their wilderness permit instead.

guides.title: Wilderness permits (overnight & backpacking)
guides.plan: Backpack or camp overnight in the wilderness
guides.summary: Any overnight stay in the wilderness needs a permit for your entry trailhead and start date. Use the seasonal reservation and pickup system, or the nearest issuing station between late October and mid-April.

facts.label: When it applies
facts.text: All year, for backpacking, overnight climbs and any other night spent in the Yosemite Wilderness, including Little Yosemite Valley and the backpacker sites by the High Sierra Camps. Day hikes (other than Half Dome), lodging and developed campgrounds do not need one.

facts.label: How to apply
facts.text: In the reservation season, choose an entry trailhead and start date and reserve on Recreation.gov (permit 445859; you need an account). The trip leader or alternate then collects the permit in person at an open wilderness center: the day before between 8 am and 5 pm, or on the start day between 8 and 11 am (until 5 pm if you asked for a late-arrival hold). The confirmation letter is not the permit. From late October to mid-April, NPS sends you to the issuing station nearest your trailhead on the day before or the day of the hike; see Winter.

facts.label: Cost
facts.text: $10 per application plus $5 per person when a permit is issued, non-refundable and non-transferable. Two people pay $20 for the trip, not per night.

facts.label: How space is allocated
facts.text: 60 percent of each trailhead's daily quota goes through a weekly lottery 24 weeks ahead: apply Sunday to Saturday, results by 5 pm Monday, accept and pay by 11:59 pm Thursday. Whatever is left opens first-come on Friday at 9 am Pacific, about 22 weeks ahead. The other 40 percent opens seven days ahead at 7 am Pacific. Reservations close three days before the start date, and each person may hold up to six active reservations.

facts.label: First 2027 lottery
facts.text: NPS calendar updated October 23 (checked October 24, 2026): apply from 12:01 am on November 8 until 11:59 pm on November 14 Pacific for the published April 30 to May 8, 2027 start window. Results by 5 pm on November 16; accept by 11:59 pm on November 19; leftover reservations released at 9 am on November 20. Later weeks have their own dates on the linked calendar. None of this confirms that a given trailhead or road will be open.

facts.label: 2027 reservation dates
facts.text: NPS trailhead calendar updated October 23 (checked October 24, 2026): Yosemite Valley and Hetch Hetchy April 30 to October 24; Wawona and Glacier Point Road May 28 to October 14; Tioga Road and Tuolumne Meadows June 18 to October 14. Outside those windows NPS lists first-come permits, still under quota. Reservation dates say nothing about road, trail or station access.

facts.label: Can I get one today?
facts.text: During the late-April to mid-October reservation season, unreserved permits are issued only in person on the start date, 8 am to 5 pm at an open wilderness center, and few if any remain; there are no after-hours permits then. From late October to mid-April, NPS says to get the permit at the nearest issuing station the day before or the day of the hike. Quotas still apply, so confirm how that station is operating.

facts.label: Winter
facts.text: Once the wilderness centers close (the Valley center from about late October to mid-April), NPS describes self-registration outside the permit station nearest your trailhead. Its winter page names Big Oak Flat, the Valley Welcome Center, Badger Pass, Wawona and Hetch Hetchy as issuing points and says there are no winter reservations. Permits remain required and quotas apply.

facts.label: Night before and after
facts.text: Anyone holding a wilderness permit or reservation may spend the night before entry and the night after exit in an open backpackers campground for $8 per person, no reservation. The Valley one, behind North Pines, follows North Pines' dates: the 2026 NPS campground table tentatively lists April 21 to October 26, while the backpackers page says about mid-April to early October.

facts.label: Not included
facts.text: Half Dome (added at pickup from an eligible trailhead), developed campgrounds, and road access. Overnight parking is banned on Tioga and Glacier Point Roads from October 15.

notices: Checked October 22, 2026: the NPS wilderness-permit page separates late-April to mid-October pickup from late-October to mid-April station permits. Guide 51.8 lists the Tuolumne Meadows Wilderness Center closing October 14 and the Valley Wilderness Center October 18, so do not assume summer counter hours. Confirm the 2026 to 2027 issuing station and self-registration arrangements for your trailhead. In winter, bear canisters are rented only at the Valley Welcome Center.

NPS current conditions updated October 21, 2026 (checked October 22): Glacier Point Road is listed open, with firefighters working nearby and no overnight parking. The Dome Fire closure east of Wawona Road, south of Glacier Point Road and north of Wawona, reaching east to the Bridalveil Creek trailhead south of the Ostrander Lake trail, remains in place. NPS says the trail to the top of Chilnualna Falls has reopened. Check the conditions page and its closure map for your route: an open road does not mean trails are open, and nothing here confirms the Ostrander Lake Trail has reopened.

guides.title: Half Dome on a backpacking trip
guides.plan: Add Half Dome to a backpacking trip
guides.summary: A wilderness permit does not cover the cables by itself. From seven eligible trailheads you can add Half Dome when you pick up the wilderness permit.

facts.label: How to add it
facts.text: Hold a wilderness permit from an eligible entry trailhead and ask for Half Dome, for all or part of the group, at pickup. Eligible entries: Happy Isles to Little Yosemite Valley; Glacier Point to Little Yosemite Valley; Happy Isles past LYV (Donohue-eligible); Sunrise Lakes; Cathedral Lakes; Rafferty Creek to Vogelsang; Mono Meadow.

facts.label: Cost
facts.text: $10 per person, paid at pickup and non-refundable, on top of the wilderness fees. Two backpackers: $20 wilderness plus $20 Half Dome, $40 in all.

facts.label: Not valid for
facts.text: Day hiking. Wilderness permits issued outside Yosemite, including JMT trips that start elsewhere, and PCT long-distance permits do not include Half Dome; those hikers use the day-hike lotteries.

facts.label: Timing and quota
facts.text: No separate advance reservation; about 75 backpacker permits a day, valid for every date on the wilderness permit.

facts.label: John Muir Trail
facts.text: A JMT trip starting in Yosemite and crossing Donohue Pass needs a Donohue-eligible permit: Happy Isles to Past LYV (15 a day, first night not in Little Yosemite Valley) or Lyell Canyon (30 a day).

notices: NPS current conditions updated October 21, 2026 (checked October 22): Glacier Point Road is listed open, with firefighters working nearby and no overnight parking. The Dome Fire closure east of Wawona Road, south of Glacier Point Road and north of Wawona, reaching east to the Bridalveil Creek trailhead south of the Ostrander Lake trail, remains in place. NPS says the trail to the top of Chilnualna Falls has reopened. Check the conditions page and its closure map; an open road does not mean trails are open, and nothing here confirms the Ostrander Lake Trail has reopened. Confirm access for the Glacier Point to Little Yosemite Valley and Mono Meadow entries before choosing either.

guides.title: Big-wall climbing permits (overnight)
guides.summary: Spending a night on a big wall requires a free wilderness climbing permit, self-issued near El Capitan Bridge before you start. Day climbs need no permit.

facts.label: How to get it
facts.text: Self-register at the kiosk by the food lockers at El Capitan Bridge, open around the clock, the day before or the day you start. Pick the listed formation, for example El Capitan–Nose, Half Dome Regular Northwest Face or Washington Column. Up to eight people per permit; talk to a climbing ranger first if there are more than four.

facts.label: Cost and quota
facts.text: Free, with no quota and no lottery.

facts.label: Where you may bivouac
facts.text: At least one pitch up a Grade V or harder route in designated wilderness, outside any closed area. Not on non-wilderness walls such as the Rostrum or Elephant Rock.

facts.label: Not included
facts.text: Campground nights. The permit does allow one night before and one after in an open backpackers campground at $8 per person. Climbing closures are a separate check.

guides.title: Campground reservations
guides.summary: Reserve or register for the specific campground before you camp. Reservation dates and release windows differ from campground to campground.

facts.label: When it applies
facts.text: Every developed-campground stay, including Camp 4 and the group and horse sites. All 13 campgrounds take reservations roughly April to October, and Upper Pines is reservation-only all year. Sleeping in a vehicle is allowed only in a site you have registered for.

facts.label: How to book
facts.text: Recreation.gov or by phone (main, TDD and outside-US numbers below), two reservations per visit or call. In winter Camp 4, Wawona and Hodgdon Meadow are first-come: register on arrival.

facts.label: Cost
facts.text: Standard sites $24 to $36 a night; Camp 4 $10 per person per night; group and horse sites priced separately. Read the total and the cancellation and no-show terms before paying.

facts.label: Release windows
facts.text: Inventory opens at 7 am Pacific and often goes within minutes. Upper, Lower and North Pines, Wawona and Hodgdon Meadow: five months ahead on the 15th (North Pines also runs a lottery). Tuolumne Meadows: half two months ahead on the 15th and half 14 days ahead. Bridalveil Creek, Crane Flat, Tamarack Flat, White Wolf, Yosemite Creek and Porcupine Flat: 14 days ahead. Camp 4: seven days ahead.

facts.label: 2026 updates
facts.text: NPS campgrounds page updated September 28, 2026: Camp 4 and Wawona Loop A stay on reservations through the night of November 28; Wawona Loops B and C close October 26; Bridalveil Creek closed on August 14 after a lightning strike.

facts.label: Can I book today?
facts.text: Only if a cancellation turns up or a first-come campground is running. This app has no live availability.

facts.label: Source conflict
facts.text: NPS's booking page (updated September 11, 2026) still shows a 2025 date range for Camp 4; the campgrounds table is used here for 2026 dates.

facts.label: Not included
facts.text: Entrance fees and wilderness nights. An entrance pass never permits sleeping in a parking lot or beside a road.

phones.label: Recreation.gov from outside the US & Canada

guides.title: California fishing license
guides.summary: Anyone 16 or older needs a California fishing licence, even for catch-and-release. It is a state licence rather than a park permit, and park rules apply on top.

facts.label: When it applies
facts.text: Everyone 16 and over who fishes in Yosemite. Younger anglers still follow the rules.

facts.label: How to buy
facts.text: CDFW online sales, a licence agent or a CDFW office; choose resident or non-resident and your dates. Short-term and temporary licences bought online must be printed.

facts.label: 2026 cost (CDFW)
facts.text: One day $21.09; two consecutive days $32.40; ten-day non-resident $64.54; 365-day resident $64.54; 365-day non-resident $174.14. Most fees include a 5 percent agent fee and a 3 percent non-refundable application fee. No refunds: CDFW treats a licence as in use from the moment of purchase.

facts.label: Can I buy one today?
facts.text: Normally yes; Yosemite runs no lottery. A 365-day licence bought online prints a temporary licence that is valid immediately for up to 30 days, and short-term licences print at checkout and start on the date you pick.

facts.label: Park rules (2026)
facts.text: All waters are open all year unless noted; year-round stream fishing is new for 2026. No bait of any kind. On the Merced, South Fork Merced, Tuolumne and their tributaries: artificial lures or flies with barbless hooks, rainbow trout catch-and-release only, brown and brook trout five a day and ten in possession. No fishing from bridges, piers or O'Shaughnessy Dam. No wading or swimming in Hetch Hetchy Reservoir.

facts.label: Source conflict
facts.text: NPS's older water-activities page (August 2023) still lists an April to November stream season; the June 2026 fishing page and the May 2026 compendium say year-round.

guides.title: Entrance fees & reservations (2026)
guides.plan: Drive or walk into the park
guides.summary: NPS says no reservation is needed to enter Yosemite in 2026. An entrance pass is still required, and it is separate from activity permits and overnight bookings.

facts.label: 2026 entry
facts.text: No entrance reservation in 2026 (NPS announcement updated February 18, 2026). That statement covers 2026 only, says nothing about 2027 and guarantees neither parking nor road access.

facts.label: Entrance pass
facts.text: Standard passes run $20 to $35: $35 per private vehicle for seven consecutive days, $30 per motorcycle. A Yosemite Annual Pass or America the Beautiful pass also covers entry. Non-US residents aged 16 and over pay an extra $100 each unless they enter on an Annual or America the Beautiful pass.

facts.label: Paying
facts.text: Cashless: cards and mobile payment only. Every entrance except Hetch Hetchy is open 24 hours.

facts.label: Not included
facts.text: Activity permits, campsites, lodging and overnight parking.

guides.title: Wedding & ceremony permits
guides.plan: Have a wedding, elopement or commitment ceremony
guides.summary: Any wedding or commitment ceremony in the park, even a tiny elopement, needs an NPS special use permit. Check the approved locations before booking anything else.

facts.label: How to apply
facts.text: Download the application, pick a site from the NPS ceremony location list and mail the original with a cheque or money order to Special Park Uses, P.O. Box 700, El Portal, CA 95318 (couriers: 5083 Foresta Rd). The form asks for a Social Security number; contact the office if you have none. After a favourable review, sign and return the prepared permit and carry the approved copy on the day.

facts.label: Timing
facts.text: More than 21 days and up to a year ahead, with no published decision time. No permits on holidays or holiday weekends, a two-hour maximum per event, and no exclusive use of any public place.

facts.label: Cost
facts.text: A $150 non-refundable application fee, plus $50 an hour for a monitor at outdoor events of roughly 30 to 50 people or more.

facts.label: Not allowed
facts.text: Decorations beyond hand-held bouquets (with limited exceptions at picnic areas), chairs, amplified music, releases of any kind including rice or birdseed, formal receptions in picnic areas, and drones.

facts.label: Not included
facts.text: Park entrance (guests pay), a California marriage licence, and concession reception venues. Ceremonies in the Yosemite Chapel are booked through its church office.

notices: An earlier NPS notice (September 25, 2026) halted October special-event applications along Glacier Point Road because of the Dome Fire. It no longer appears on the page updated October 9 and checked October 25. That does not prove applications or sites are available again; ask Special Park Uses about your date and place.

guides.title: Scattering cremated remains
guides.summary: Get a written authorisation letter before scattering cremated human remains, then keep to its conditions.

facts.label: How to apply
facts.text: Download the application and email it to the Office of Special Park Uses, then wait for the written authorisation. Nothing is processed until the original application arrives.

facts.label: Conditions
facts.text: Out of sight of roads, trails, paths and parking; at least 100 yards from any watercourse or creek bed, wet or dry; spread widely; no marker or identification disc left behind; no scattering from the air; no commercial scattering for profit. Any state permission is your own responsibility.

facts.label: Cost
facts.text: Not stated on the NPS page that was checked; ask the office rather than assuming it is free.

facts.label: Timing
facts.text: No processing time or daily limit is published; ask about your date before making plans.

facts.label: Book of Memories
facts.text: The Yosemite Chapel keeps a Book of Memories; call the chapel for details.

guides.title: Special events & gatherings
guides.summary: Organised events, religious gatherings, ceremonies, large group camps and similar uses need a special use permit. There is no single headcount that triggers it.

facts.label: How to apply
facts.text: Mail the original Special Park Use application and fee to Special Park Uses, describing the activity, dates, place, attendance and equipment. Insurance, often $1 million per occurrence, may be required; serving alcohol needs prior approval and liquor liability cover.

facts.label: Timing
facts.text: At least 30 days and no more than six months ahead. The Lower River Amphitheater is often booked months out in summer.

facts.label: Cost
facts.text: A $100 non-refundable processing fee plus cost recovery for staff time, monitoring and overhead. Applying grants nothing by itself.

facts.label: Not included
facts.text: Weddings, which have their own rules, and entrance fees.

notices: NPS weddings page updated September 25, 2026: no further applications for October special events along the Glacier Point Road corridor because of Dome Fire suppression.

guides.title: Demonstrations, marches & printed matter
guides.plan: Hold a demonstration or hand out literature
guides.summary: Groups of 25 or fewer may use the designated First Amendment areas without a permit. Larger demonstrations, marches of any size and advance area reservations need one, and marches are allowed only in the Yosemite Village Mall pedestrian area.

facts.label: Permit needed for
facts.text: Demonstrations by more than 25 people; selling or handing out printed material by more than 25 people; marches and parades of any size; reserving a designated area in advance.

facts.label: Marches and parades
facts.text: The May 2026 compendium bans them everywhere except the Yosemite Village Mall pedestrian area between the Exploration Center and the Valley Welcome Center (not the bike path beside it), and even there a permit is required at any size.

facts.label: Designated areas
facts.text: Near the Valley shuttle stop on the way to the visitor center, beside the Wawona Store and by the day-use parking near O'Shaughnessy Dam; plus, 8 am to 5 pm when not otherwise in use, outside the Yosemite Chapel, at the Lower Pines and Lower River amphitheaters and outside the Valley Visitor Center Theater.

facts.label: How and cost
facts.text: Use the First Amendment Activities application rather than the general event form; permits run up to 14 days. There is no fee, and parks have up to 10 days to act on a fully completed application under the NPS national rule.

facts.label: Source conflict
facts.text: Yosemite's special-use page says groups of '25, or more' need a permit while '25 individuals, or less' do not; the May 2026 compendium says more than 25. Ask Special Park Uses about a group of exactly 25.

guides.title: Filming, photography & audio
guides.summary: Most small, low-impact filming and photography needs no permit. Larger crews, staging, exclusive use or productions in wilderness need to be checked with NPS first.

facts.label: Usually no permit
facts.text: Eight or fewer people, in areas open to the public, with hand-carried gear, no exclusive use, no resource impact and no added NPS administrative cost, whether the work is commercial, personal, student, news or content creation.

facts.label: Permit or review
facts.text: More than eight people, sets or staging, exclusive or closed-area use, other impacts, or anything beyond casual filming in wilderness (which needs a permit at any group size). Contact the coordinator first to confirm and to choose the short or long application.

facts.label: Timing
facts.text: At least 30 days for a complete, simple request and at least 90 days for projects that need environmental, cultural or tribal review.

facts.label: Cost
facts.text: Application, location and monitoring charges plus insurance, generally $1 million of liability cover, may apply. The NPS page mixes overlapping fee tables, so ask for a written estimate.

facts.label: Not included
facts.text: Drones, which are not permitted, and paid photography workshops, which need a commercial use authorisation.

guides.title: Commercial use authorization (CUA)
guides.plan: Offer paid guiding, tours or transport
guides.summary: Businesses and individuals selling services in the park need a commercial use authorisation (CUA). Visitors who book an authorised operator do not apply for it, though they may still need their own permits.

facts.label: When it applies
facts.text: Paid goods or services that happen at least partly inside the park and use park resources: guiding, backcountry hiking, photo and fishing instruction, stock rides, tours, transport, chain fitting and sales, hang gliding and the other services on the linked NPS list (checked October 25, 2026).

facts.label: How to apply
facts.text: Through the NPS online CUA Application and Reporting System. NPS opened the general 2027 window on October 15, 2026 and closes it on September 1, 2027; service-specific exceptions have their own dates.

facts.label: Cost
facts.text: For 2027, $350 for a first application and $250 for later applications to the same park in the same calendar year, non-refundable. Management fees and entrance fees are extra.

facts.label: Exception windows
facts.text: NPS's 2027 page lists chain fitting and chain sales applications from November 1, 2026 to June 15, 2027, and hang-gliding applications from June 1, 2026 to October 15, 2027. These are operator application dates, not visitor bookings or flight approvals.

facts.label: Timing
facts.text: Allow at least 45 days for a complete application, reviewed in the order received; approval is not guaranteed.

facts.label: Annual report
facts.text: Reports for the previous calendar year are due February 28, 2027, and the management fee is due two weeks after the report is accepted. Late reports or payments can suspend the current CUA.

facts.label: Visitors
facts.text: A CUA does not stand in for the wilderness or Half Dome permits the people on the trip need.

guides.title: Research & specimen collecting
guides.summary: Scientific research and specimen collecting go through the NPS Research Permit and Reporting System. It is not a route to souvenir collecting.

facts.label: How to apply
facts.text: Create an investigator account in RPRS, choose Yosemite, fill in the study, locations, team and data details and attach supporting documents. Answer the coordinator's questions and carry the signed permit in the field.

facts.label: Timing
facts.text: Apply at least 90 days before fieldwork; restricted locations, sensitive resources or tribal consultation take longer.

facts.label: Cost
facts.text: No Yosemite fee schedule appears on the pages checked; ask the coordinator about costs and curation.

sources.label: NPS: apply for a research permit
NPS Research Permit and Reporting System

guides.title: Hang gliding
guides.summary: Hang gliding happens only by permit at designated sites, arranged through the NPS-linked Yosemite Hang Gliding Association. Paragliding and BASE jumping are not allowed.

facts.label: How it works
facts.text: The association, which is not a government site, asks pilots rated H4 or higher to claim dates on its calendar, wait for an approved monitor to confirm, and contact that monitor before travelling. The monitor clears flights with park dispatch. Launch is from the designated areas at Glacier Point and landing is in Leidig Meadow.

facts.label: Can I fly today?
facts.text: No. A requested date is not an approved flight, and this is not a beginner or walk-up activity.

facts.label: Cost
facts.text: Not published on the association page; ask about charges, membership and insurance.

sources.label: Yosemite Hang Gliding Association (NPS-linked, not a government site)

guides.title: Educational entrance-fee waiver
guides.plan: Bring a school or research group
guides.summary: Accredited educational and scientific groups can ask for entrance fees to be waived for a trip tied to Yosemite's resources. It is not an activity permit.

facts.label: How to apply
facts.text: Email the signed Entrance Fee Waiver for Resource Education Study form, proof of accreditation or tax-exempt status and a one-page lesson plan to yose_fee_waiver@nps.gov at least two weeks ahead. Email only; late requests may not be handled.

facts.label: On the day
facts.text: Every vehicle needs a copy of the approved waiver at the gate, or the normal fee applies.

facts.label: Group limits
facts.text: Day-hiking groups in wilderness are capped at 35 people on trail and 8 off trail.

facts.label: Not included
facts.text: Camping, collecting or other restricted activities, and commercial tour groups.

guides.title: Other park permissions
guides.summary: Case-by-case permissions named in the Superintendent's Compendium. A mention of a permit does not mean one is available on request.

facts.label: Wood cutting
facts.text: A permit is required at the Wawona, Hodgdon, Foresta, White Wolf and Valley wood lots; call the Administrative Support Office in Mariposa. This is separate from gathering dead and down wood for a legal campfire.

facts.label: Oversize vehicles
facts.text: Exceeding posted load, weight or size limits needs a permit review, and some roads cannot take the vehicle at all. It is not a way around an RV that is over a road's limit.

facts.label: Hetch Hetchy after hours
facts.text: The road is open from sunrise to sunset (civil twilight); any other use is by permit only. Ask NPS before planning, since a wilderness permit does not open the gate.

facts.label: Large wilderness displays
facts.text: Flags, banners or signs over 15 square feet, alone or combined, need authorisation in wilderness; ask Special Park Uses.

facts.label: Rights-of-way
facts.text: Utilities and telecommunications apply through the NPS Right-of-Way Permit Application Portal.

facts.label: Specialist uses
facts.text: Aircraft deliveries or wreck removal, explosives or fireworks, public-address systems, livestock, construction and similar uses are listed in the compendium; ask NPS for the application route and decision timeline.

guides.title: Day hiking & sightseeing
guides.summary: Day use needs no wilderness permit, including Glacier Point, Mariposa Grove, Yosemite Falls, Cathedral Lakes and Clouds Rest. The Half Dome cables are the one named exception.

facts.label: Still check
facts.text: Trail closures and conditions, wilderness group limits (35 on trail, 8 off trail), overnight stays, events and commercial services each have their own rules. This is the park-wide day-hike rule, not a live check that a trail is open.

facts.label: Day climbing
facts.text: Day climbs, and watching climbers, need no wilderness climbing permit; check climbing closures.

links.label: Valley day hikes in Trails & camping

guides.title: Boating & rafting
guides.summary: The NPS boating page describes no general permit for personal day boating. Check the permitted river sections, launch sites and life-jacket rules instead.

facts.label: Rules
facts.text: Launch only where permitted; no trailers or wheeled launching; no dragging boats across vegetation. Everyone aboard must wear a life jacket in some conditions and carry one otherwise. Overnight river trips need a wilderness permit.

facts.label: Prohibited
facts.text: Boating and swimming in Hetch Hetchy Reservoir, a public drinking-water supply, and swimming at Emerald Pool and Silver Apron above Vernal Fall.

facts.label: Valley launch sites
facts.text: NPS's boating page (June 2022) allows launching and take-out on the Valley rafting sections only at the signed areas by Clark's, Stoneman and El Capitan bridges and on the sandy, unvegetated part of Sentinel Beach. Sections open and close day by day with the river level; check that page and the signs before launching.

facts.label: Raft rentals
facts.text: Renting a raft at Curry Village, seasonal and dependent on river conditions, is not a park permit and changes none of these rules.

guides.title: Drones, BASE jumping & paragliding
guides.summary: Launching, landing or flying a drone from park land or water is prohibited, and the park issues no drone permits. BASE jumping is prohibited, and paragliders are excluded from hang-gliding authorisations.

facts.label: Note
facts.text: An FAA credential or commercial status is not park permission. Drones are also barred at permitted weddings.

guides.title: Campfires
guides.summary: No permit, but campfire rules and seasonal fire restrictions apply, and a camping reservation never overrides a restriction.

facts.label: Campgrounds
facts.text: Fires only in a fire ring and never unattended; in the Yosemite Valley campgrounds and Hodgdon Meadow only between 5 and 10 pm.

facts.label: Restrictions
facts.text: NPS uses three stages: below 6,000 feet, below 8,000 feet, and park-wide. Check the current NPS restriction before lighting anything; this saved guide does not tell you the active stage or give permission to burn.

guides.title: Collecting rocks, plants or artifacts
guides.plan: Take home a rock or pine cone
guides.summary: Souvenir collecting is not allowed. The research permit process is not a visitor workaround, and the limited food and wood exceptions are defined separately.

facts.label: Examples
facts.text: NPS lists collecting plants (pine cones included), reptiles or butterflies, picking up archaeological or historic objects such as arrowheads, and using metal detectors to find historic items among the illegal acts it asks visitors to report.

fireNotice: NPS current conditions, updated Oct 21, 2026 (checked Oct 22): Glacier Point Road is listed open, with firefighters working nearby and no overnight parking. The Dome Fire area east of Wawona Road, south of Glacier Point Road and north of Wawona, extending east to the Bridalveil Creek trailhead (south of the Ostrander Lake trail), remains closed. NPS says the trail to the top of Chilnualna Falls has reopened. Check the current conditions page and its official closure map for your route; an open road does not establish trail access, and this notice does not confirm Ostrander Lake Trail reopening.
